stop_location.description: A stop is a run of observations inside a 150 m band either side of the island's OneMap shoreline for at least 120 s: stops are 'at Island X', not at a named jetty. The harbour/jetty reference (data/reference/harbours/) is not used.

clock_correction.method: per device-day median of database_time - collection_time; a +5 h shift is applied only to device-days whose difference is consistent and within tolerance of 18000 s
clock_correction.evidence_summary: 0 of 47027 device-days show a consistent difference near 5 h; 0 of 17233072 observations corrected. National median difference 2.0 s, p99 34672.9 s; no 5 h cluster separates from the long tail of delayed uploads.
clock_correction.statement: no time correction applied: no device-day met the offset criteria; pending organiser confirmation of the timezone of both time fields

clock_exclusion.note: excluded journeys stay in the private trip/journey tables and in service_edges.csv; they are not used to form regular services

speed_unit_status: consistent with knots, pending organiser confirmation

speed_unit_check.note: consistent with knots (derived km/h / raw speed is about 1.9, 1 knot = 1.852 km/h), pending organiser confirmation

stop_location_mode_options.island_shoreline: a stop is at the island: a run inside a band of radius_m either side of the island's OneMap shoreline. Harbour reference, jetty points and jetty verification are not read.
stop_location_mode_options.jetty: a stop is within radius_m of a verified jetty point (shoreline band only for islands without one, flagged no_jetty_point). Kept for later; outputs may then carry jetty ids.

stops.note: PROVISIONAL. radius_m is the shoreline band width (m) in island_shoreline mode (the default). A stop is a run of consecutive observations of one trajectory inside that band (or, in jetty mode, within radius_m of a verified jetty) lasting at least dwell_seconds. A gap longer than stop_gap_flag_seconds inside a run marks the stop unconfirmed; nothing is filled or interpolated. Runs never cross a trajectory split or a non-accepted transition.

classification.note: PROVISIONAL, taken from FollowMe_pipeline/boat_filter.py and boat_types.py (speedboat p90 >= 18 kn, slow < 14 kn, 14-18 reported as mixed). Speed is derived from accepted movement segments (km/h / kmh_per_knot), not the raw field. A path of >= 2 km of consecutive accepted moving segments replaces the original 2 km straight-line sea run. Land share is estimated on a deterministic sample of observations per device. Classes are review hints and never filter rows.

services.note: PROVISIONAL. Departures at the first stop are clustered within departure_window_minutes; a cluster seen on >= min_days_regular distinct days is a regular service. A shorter signature matches a longer canonical route when it keeps the same order and omits at most max_skipped_stops stops.

coverage.note: PROVISIONAL. A date has good coverage when regional active devices >= min_day_device_ratio x the monthly median and at least min_site_devices distinct devices were seen near the signature's stops. Otherwise 'not observed' says little.

disclosure.note: No exported row may be backed by fewer than both minima. Per-date device counts below the device minimum are shown as '<3'.

clock_thresholds.note: EVERY threshold in this file is PROVISIONAL. They were set by reading the national distribution of database_time minus collection_time, not validated against ground truth. The organisers have not confirmed the timezone of either time field.
clock_thresholds.difference_definition: database_time minus collection_time, in seconds, per retained observation (reporting_lag_seconds is NULL in gps_clean.parquet while the timezone is unconfirmed, so the difference is computed from the two timestamps)

local.note: device-day median difference near 0 or a small positive reporting lag

offset_5h.note: device-day median within this distance of expected_offset_seconds AND consistent (below)

consistency.note: a non-local offset only counts as a clock offset when at least this share of the device-day's observations lie within window_seconds of the device-day median. A median drifting up through hours with a wide spread is delayed or buffered upload, not a clock offset.

device.note: a device has a stable class when at least min_measured_days device-days were measured (class local/offset_5h/other) and at least min_share_same_class of them agree. Device-days that are unknown (too few observations or inconsistent difference) inherit a stable device class; otherwise they stay unknown.

clock_thresholds.exclude_note: Devices classed unknown or other stay in every table but their journeys are not used to form regular services (override with --clock-exclude).

disclosure_rule.note: No exported row may be backed by fewer than both minima. Per-date device counts below the device minimum are shown as '<3'.
disclosure_rule.rule: no exported row is backed by fewer than the minimum distinct devices AND distinct days; per-date device counts below the device minimum print as '<N'

labels: Output labels are 'inferred class' and 'inferred service'. Nothing here is a confirmed ferry, official timetable, passenger service or specific vessel.
